comparison.objective: Fit and orient a split-core current sensor around exactly one correct conductor; candidate adjusts, locks, and validates a robot-axis shock absorber.
comparison.physical_skill: Sensor task tests grasping a hinged device, selecting one conductor, orienting polarity, seating it, and closing its jaw. Candidate tests recessed tool insertion, setscrew loosening/tightening, counterheld fine collar rotation, control actuation, and iterative tuning from impact response. Shared alignment and closure are generic.
comparison.success_condition: Sensor success requires line-only enclosure, jaw ≤5°, arrow within 25° toward the load, release, and stillness. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J cycles, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike, and retained setting. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, drift, and locking-torque limits.
comparison.reason: Correct conductor selection, polarity, and hinged-jaw closure do not test mechanical parameter tuning or lock retention under subsequent dynamic loading.
